A gateway to Web3

Web3 has a first-mile problem. Before you have learned anything you are asked to create an account, install a wallet, fund it, sign an approval you cannot read, and pay for the privilege of finding out what a slippage setting does. DexLadder removes that mile entirely.

Last verified 16 September 2026 · written by the DexLadder team

The entry problem, stated plainly

Every on-chain skill worth having — reading pool depth, pricing an order against a curve, understanding why a position was liquidated, seeing what an approval actually grants — is currently taught by taking money from people who do not yet have those skills. The tuition is paid to sandwich bots, to bad fills, to liquidation cascades and to contracts nobody read. That is an absurd way to run an on-ramp, and it is the single biggest reason most people bounce off Web3 and never come back.

The whole on-chain surface, in one place

  • AMM mechanics — Uniswap v2 constant product, v3 concentrated liquidity, Curve StableSwap and staking, running the contracts' own arithmetic rather than a teaching approximation.
  • Live DEX pools — depth, fee tier, impact curve and token safety checks, cross-checked against a second independent source.
  • Chain data — blocks, transactions, wallets and transfers, beside the chart rather than in another tab.
  • Your own contracts — point the terminal at your own Anvil or Hardhat node and route real, node-signed orders into a pool you deployed.
  • Derivatives — perpetuals with index-mark liquidation, maintenance margin and funding charged every interval.
  • Automation — build a strategy with no code, or connect the bot you already wrote in any language.
  • The part nobody prepares for — a tax ledger covering four jurisdictions, computed on your own device.

Microstructure, which is where the money actually goes

A gateway that hands you a buy button teaches you nothing about what pressing it costs. Two mechanisms carry most of that cost, and both are modelled here rather than described.

The first is the order book. Forty levels a side sit around the live mid, and the liquidity in them is anchored to the asset's own 24-hour volume, so depth and spread differ between a major and a microcap the way they do in the market. Your order walks the ladder and pays each level it takes; the liquidity it consumes is really gone and heals over about six seconds; a resting limit waits behind the size already queued at its price instead of filling the moment the price grazes it; and anything larger than the book fills what exists and rests or cancels by its time-in-force. Watching your own average fill drift away from the price you clicked is the fastest way to understand position sizing.

The second is MEV. Opt into the sandwich bots and a pool swap becomes a target — but only on the real condition: when your slippage tolerance is loose enough to be worth taking and the bot's profit clears both legs' pool fees plus two high-priority swaps of gas. The preview shows the clean price and the sandwiched price side by side, and the fill matches the prediction exactly. Gas sits beside it with priority tiers, live congestion, and the three fates a transaction actually meets — included, pending until it drifts and reverts, or dropped — with the fee paid either way. This is the part of on-chain trading that costs beginners the most and is explained to them the least.

Keyless is the architecture, not a feature

There is no account, no server-side profile, no wallet connection and no key input anywhere in the product. Everything — balances, positions, the journal, the tax ledger — is computed and stored in your own browser. That is why there is nothing to breach, nothing to sell, no engagement machinery and no deposit button. It is also why the honest limits are what they are: nothing syncs between devices, and clearing browser storage clears your history.

Where the real thing begins

This is not a walled garden that ends at a paywall. The skills transfer directly: the order you sized here is sized the same way with a real wallet; the pool you priced here is priced by the same curve on-chain; the approval you learned to distrust here is the same approval that drains people. When you do open a wallet, you open it knowing what you are looking at — which is the entire point of a gateway.

Questions people actually ask

Do I need a wallet to use DexLadder?

No. There is no wallet connection anywhere in the product, and no key or seed phrase is ever requested. You can explore live on-chain markets, AMM pools and chain data without connecting anything.

Is this a real Web3 app or a mock-up?

The data and the mechanics are real — live markets, live pool reserves, the contracts' own curve arithmetic, and a fork sandbox that sends node-signed transactions to your own chain. Only the capital in the trading desk is simulated.

What does it cost?

Nothing. No paid tier, no advertising, no affiliate exchange links and no token.

Open the desk — free, no account — no account, nothing to install

DexLadder is a free, keyless gateway to Web3 — live on-chain markets, real AMM mechanics, derivatives, strategy bots and your own contracts. No account, no wallet connection, no key ever requested.
